clue.text: Freshly made bean soup may be served

definitions.note: describes a legal document that is delivered formally to someone, standing for the document itself

indicators.note: something freshly made has been newly put together, so these letters are assembled anew in another order

explanation.surface: A cook announces that newly prepared bean soup is ready to be dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly made' reworks BEAN SOUP. 'May be served' looks like the soup being dished out, but a writ is what gets served.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal summons is a document that is formally served on the person named in it.

clue.text: Vital point in game between numbers of Romans

indicators.note: the game sits between the two Roman figures, which flank it on either side

parts.note: C (100) and X (10) are Roman numerals
RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the key moment of a match came between two Roman scores.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (Rugby Union) goes between C and X, two Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The crux of a matter is its essential, decisive point.

clue.text: One who foils trespassers?

parts.note: reads as a swordsman wielding a foil, but means someone who puts up barriers to keep intruders out

explanation.surface: A sword-fighter seems to be holding off intruders with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: A foil is a fencing sword, but 'foils' is also to thwart: whoever builds boundary barriers thwarts trespassers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who erects fences keeps trespassers out, and a swordsman with a foil is also so named.

clue.text: Big egg producer from nothing, on the way to be wealthy

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
ST is street, a way
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A rags-to-riches story about someone starting from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big egg producer' sounds like a poultry farmer, but it is the bird that lays the largest eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich lays the largest egg of any living bird.

clue.text: Involved in a fraud, but remaining confident

indicators.note: involved means intricately tangled, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mixed up in a scam stays calm and self-assured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' tangles IN A FRAUD; 'but remaining' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without fear is a close synonym of feeling confident and assured.

clue.text: A beef drink prepared and used in the kitchen

definitions.note: describes an implement found in the kitchen, standing for the implement itself

indicators.note: fodder that is prepared has been worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe for a beefy drink to be made up at the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' rearranges A BEEF DRINK; the definition describes rather than names the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated blade for slicing loaves is a standard kitchen utensil.

clue.text: Affected type from the Paris model agency?

definitions.text: Affected type from the Paris model agency?

parts.words: Affected type from the Paris model agency?
parts.note: the French word for someone who poses suggests a model on the books of a Paris agency, but in English it means a pretentious show-off

explanation.surface: A snooty character seems to have come from a French modelling agency.
explanation.walkthrough: In French the word means one who poses, like a model; in English it is someone who strikes attitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretentious person who adopts an affected manner to impress others is called this.

clue.text: Digs for foreign coins

definitions.meaning: digs is informal British for lodgings, a place to live
American and Canadian 25-cent pieces bear this name

explanation.surface: Someone excavates in search of overseas money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like a verb but is British slang for lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodgings are living accommodation, and coins worth a fourth of a dollar share the name.

clue.text: Thin pointed weapon

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass, so the point here gives that letter
an arrow is a weapon

explanation.surface: A slender sharp-tipped weapon such as a dart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointed' gives N, a compass point, before ARROW; the surface reads it as describing the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thin or slim is of small width, which is the adjective's sense here.

clue.text: Top primate gets the vote

parts.note: an ape is a primate
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: The leading monkey wins an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top primate' looks like one phrase, but 'Top' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The summit or highest point of something is its peak or top.

clue.text: Out of clean forks? Use a spoon to eat these

definitions.text: Use a spoon to eat these

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: With no clean forks left, someone must spoon up their breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' scrambles CLEAN FORKS; 'of' is a link. The surface makes 'Out of' mean having none left.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakfast cereal of toasted maize flakes is eaten from a bowl with a spoon.

clue.text: North African halves a number, then doubles it

indicators.note: the half kept is then written twice in succession
halving the word keeps its second half only

parts.note: taken as the word number

explanation.surface: Arithmetic instructions: halve a figure, then double it back.
explanation.walkthrough: Halve the word NUMBER to get BER, then double it. The surface reads like sums that return you to where you started.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berbers are indigenous peoples of North Africa, so a member is a North African.

clue.text: Boat train being derailed

indicators.note: a derailed train comes off its tracks in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A boat train has come off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boat train' looks like a single phrase, but 'Boat' is the definition and 'derailed' scrambles TRAIN BEING.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing vessel of this type is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Nutty biscuits

definitions.meaning: thin dry savoury biscuits, eaten with cheese

explanation.surface: A description of nut-flavoured biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutty' seems to describe the biscuits but means mad, a separate sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad, and also the name for thin crisp savoury biscuits.

clue.text: Stays if made content

definitions.note: a verb here, to make someone happy enough

indicators.note: letters that are made into something are reformed, so these are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone will stay only if they are kept happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' rearranges STAYS IF; 'content' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To content someone is to please or gratify them, meeting their wishes.

clue.text: It's extremely difficult, but it's finished anyway

indicators.note: anyway suggests in any manner at all, so these letters are put in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A tough task has been completed regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyway' rearranges FINISHED; 'It's' and 'but it's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle described as devilishly hard or fiendish is extremely difficult.

clue.text: Poet and MP is an odd combination

indicators.note: a combination joins things in a new arrangement, so these letters are recombined

explanation.surface: A poet who is also a politician makes a strange pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combination' mixes IS AN ODD. Joseph Addison (1672-1719) was an English poet, essayist and Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was an English writer of verse who also sat in Parliament.

clue.text: Being prejudiced is only right, say

definitions.meaning: having just one of its two faces, such as only the right

explanation.surface: Someone claims their bias is simply justified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like 'correct', but it is the right-hand side, an example of a single side.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased view favours one party; something with only a right-hand face has one face only.

clue.text: Drag along to wild parties

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is hauled off reluctantly to rowdy gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' scrambles PARTIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk wearily or reluctantly is to trudge or drag along.

clue.text: A weather-beaten bird

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A bird battered by the elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather-beaten' reads as one word, but 'beaten' rearranges A WEATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A small migratory songbird with a white rump is a wheatear.

clue.text: Bad luck on Robin getting two ducks

parts.note: Robin Hood, the outlaw of English legend
a duck is a zero score in cricket, written O; two give OO

explanation.surface: Misfortune strikes Robin when he is out for nought twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batsman's score of nought; the surface pictures Robin failing twice at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx, something that brings bad luck.

clue.text: Angled and he'd caught a fish

indicators.note: he'd catches the fish, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as the letters of he'd without the apostrophe
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fisherman went angling and landed a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angled' suggests fishing but means tilted; HE'D holds EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has heeled over is tilted at an angle, leaning to one side.

clue.text: Has inherent desire for animals

indicators.note: the desire is inherent in Has, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Someone has an innate craving for animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has inherent desire' reads as a single statement about someone's nature; 'for' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are carnivorous African and Asian animals.

clue.text: Signing-on points

parts.note: suggests where the unemployed register, but means the row of dots where a signature goes

explanation.surface: Places where people register for benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signing-on' in British usage means registering as unemployed; here it is literally signing on a form.
explanation.definitionFit: A form marks where to sign with a row of printed dots.

clue.text: Article about Kipling poem of unaffected simplicity

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the article is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: An essay on a Kipling poem praises its plain innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article about' suggests an essay on a topic, but 'about' is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive or artless people show an unaffected, innocent simplicity.

clue.text: A sound record

explanation.surface: A sound recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound record' looks like a reliable record or audio record.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tone is a sound, and to jot something down is to record it.

clue.text: Bay horses

parts.note: reads as horses of a reddish-brown colour, but means any horses ridden

explanation.surface: Reddish-brown horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a colour, but the clue just wants horses one rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses that people ride are called their mounts.

clue.text: Glance at the fixtures — not much on

definitions.note: describes skimpy underwear, standing for the garments

parts.note: to scan is to glance over quickly
ties are sporting fixtures, matches

explanation.surface: Someone looks over the match list and finds little happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not much on' sounds like few matches scheduled, but means wearing little: SCANTIES are skimpy knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy women's underwear leaves the wearer with very little on.
